rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claims that the saved are kept far away and do not hear Hell concern its punishment and do not negate their entry into it.
rows.anchor: فأما الذين تمسكوا بقوله تعالى : { أولئك عنها مبعدون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports establish that reckoning occurs on earth, or where earth will be; since Hell is near earth and Paradise in heaven, people gather at reckoning, enter Hell, then God raises the saved and sends the people of Fire into it.
rows.anchor: قلنا : ثبت بالأخبار أن المحاسبة تكون في الأرض أو حيث كانت الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥatm is the verbal noun of ḥatama, to make something binding; the decreed thing is called ḥatm, as in the expressions خلق الله and ضرب الأسير.
rows.anchor: الحتم مصدر حتم الأمر إذا أوجبه فسمى المحتوم بالحتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who make punishment rationally obligatory argue that على signals obligation here, whereas what is established only by reports is not called obligatory.
rows.anchor: واحتج من أوجب العقاب عقلا فقال : إن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promise cannot be subject to failure, so what He promises functions as though it were obligatory.
rows.anchor: وعد الله تعالى لما استحال تطرق الخلف إليه جرى مجرى الواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ننجى is reported with three forms, each described here as passive: ننجي, وننجي, وينجي.
rows.anchor: قرىء ننجي وننجي وينجي على ما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi argues that everyone enters Hell, only the God-fearing are saved, and the sinful are not God-fearing; therefore grave sinners remain in Hell forever.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : الآية دالة على قولنا في الوعيد لأن الله تعالى بين أن الكل يردونها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas defines the God-fearing person here as one who avoids associating partners with God by saying there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : المتقي هو الذي اتقى الشرك بقول لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi endorses Ibn Abbas: every believer in God and His messengers avoids shirk and is therefore a muttaqi; the grave sinner is included and must eventually leave Hell under the verse's general promise.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الذي قاله ابن عباس هو الحق الذي يشهد الدليل بصحته

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi also claims the verse rules out accountable people who are in neither Paradise nor Hell.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : وتدل الآية أيضا ، على فساد قول من يقول : إن من المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says the God-fearing are saved but does not specify that they are saved into Paradise; even if it did, a third group with balanced obedience and disobedience could remain, so exclusion of that group needs another proof.
rows.anchor: هذا ضعيف لأن الآية تدل على أنه تعالى ينجي الذين اتقوا وليس فيها ما يدل على أنه ينجيهم إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: من المعتزلة
rows.claim: Some Muʿtazilites use the definite plural الظالمين as a general expression to support the doctrine of the threat; Razi says discussion of general forms has been treated earlier.
rows.anchor: ومن المعتزلة من تمسك في الوعيد بقوله : { ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا }

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf takes ورود as kneeling around Hell: believers leave the unbelievers for Paradise after rescue, while unbelievers remain kneeling in place.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) قوله : { ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا } دليل على أن المراد بالورود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh polytheists argued that if the believers were right, their worldly life should be better; a wise God would not abase devoted allies and favor those who turn away, so the reverse worldly fortunes supposedly disproved the believers.
rows.anchor: لو كنتم أنتم على الحق وكنا على الباطل لكان حالكم في الدنيا أحسن وأطيب من حالنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is reported that the unbelievers adorned their hair and clothes, perfumed themselves, then boasted to poor Muslims that they were more honored by God.
rows.anchor: ويروى أنهم كانوا يرجلون شعورهم ويدهنون ويتطيبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of bayyināt is articulated wording with clear meanings, either decisive verses or ambiguous ones clarified by decisive verses or by the Prophet's speech or actions.
rows.anchor: أنها مرتلات الألفاظ مبينات المعاني إما محكمات أو متشابهات فقد تبعها البيان بالمحكمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the verses are manifestly miraculous: they challenged opponents, who could not produce a rival.
rows.anchor: أنها ظاهرات الإعجاز تحدى بها فما قدروا على معارضتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation takes them as plain proofs admitting no question or objection, like the proof of resurrection in this surah.
rows.anchor: دلائل ظاهرة واضحة لا يتوجه عليها سؤال ولا اعتراض مثل قوله تعالى في إثبات صحة الحشر

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads maqāman with ḍamma, meaning a place of residence or dwelling.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير : { مقاما } بالضم وهو موضع الإقامة والمنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers use fatḥa, taking maqāman as a place of standing.
rows.anchor: والباقون بالفتح وهو موضع القيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadī means an assembly or gathering place; its forms include nadī and nādī and its plural is andiyah, as in two cited verses.
rows.anchor: يقال : ندى وناد ، والجمع الأندية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb nadawtu means I gathered people in the assembly; Dar al-Nadwa in Mecca was so named because people assembled there.
rows.anchor: ويقال : ندوت القوم أندوهم إذا جمعتهم في المجلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples enjoyed even greater worldly blessings yet God destroyed them; this disproves either that worldly prosperity proves divine favor or that God's beloved cannot suffer worldly grief.
rows.anchor: إن من كان أعظم نعمة منكم في الدنيا قد أهلكهم الله تعالى وأبادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A generation is a people of an age in relation to those who come after, because they precede them; أحسن is accusative as an adjective of كم.
rows.anchor: أهل كل عصر قرن لمن بعدهم لأنهم يتقدمونهم وهم أحسن في محل النصب صفة لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athāth means household furnishings.
rows.anchor: والأثاث متاع البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One r-āʾ reading with a silent hamza followed by yāʾ means appearance or form, on the pattern of a passive participle from رأيت.
rows.anchor: بهمزة ساكنة بعدها ياء وهو المنظر والهيئة فعل بمعنى مفعول من رأيت رئيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another r-āʾ reading, ريئا, has metathesis, like راء from رأى.
rows.anchor: ريئا على القلب كقولهم راء في رأى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A doubled-yāʾ r-āʾ reading comes from changing hamza to yāʾ and assimilating, or from الري meaning luxury and well-being.
rows.anchor: بالياء المشددة على قلب الهمزة ياء ، والإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further yāʾ reading deletes hamza from ريئا and transfers its vowel to the preceding quiescent yāʾ.
rows.anchor: بالياء على حذف الهمزة رأسا ووجهه أن يخفف المقلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The zāy reading زيا derives from zayy, a collection of adornments; the phrase then means they looked better than these people.
rows.anchor: وأما بالزاي المنقطة من فوق زيا فاشتقاقه من الزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a second answer, even if the misguided receive prolonged worldly ease, it ends in punishment in this life or the next; worldly blessings cannot save them.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن هذا الجواب الثاني عن تلك الشبهة وتقريره لنفرض أن هذا الضال المتنعم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worse place answers their boast of a better dwelling, while weaker troops answers their boast of a finer gathering; they will learn their company cannot defend them in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فقوله : { فسيعلمون من هو شر مكانا } مذكور في مقابلة قولهم : { خير مقاما }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compelled-sounding imperative falyamdud means God gives respite and lengthens life; its command form signals that this outcome is inevitable and removes their excuses.
rows.anchor: مد له الرحمن أي أمهله وأملى له في العمر فأخرج على لفظ الأمر إيذانا بوجوب ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At judgment the prolonged sinner will be asked whether God gave him a lifetime in which to reflect.
rows.anchor: ويقال له يوم القيامة : { أو لم * نعمركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording also resembles the statement that respite is granted so people may increase in sin.
rows.anchor: وكقولهم : { إنما نملى لهم ليزدادوا إثما }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported interpretation of punishment before the Hour is punishment in the grave.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يكون هو عذاب القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is the punishment they face when they see death and their fate directly.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون هو العذاب الذي سيكون عند المعاينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is a reversal in worldly circumstances from honor to humiliation, wealth to poverty, health to illness, and safety to fear.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أيضا أن يكون المراد تغير أحوالهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation is that the believers gain power over them.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون المراد تسليط المؤمنين عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment may refer specifically to what happened to them at Badr.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أيضا أن يكون المراد ما نالهم يوم بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Increasing guidance is rationally possible because one kind of knowledge or guidance may depend on another; faith can precede and enable sincerity, which is further guidance.
rows.anchor: لا يبعد أن يكون بعض أنواع الاهتداء مشروطا بالبعض فإن حاصل الاهتداء يرجع إلى العلم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret the increase in guidance as an increase in reward for prior guidance.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من حمل الزيادة في الهدى على الثواب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others interpret the increase as acts of worship that follow from faith.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من فسر هذه الزيادة بالعبادات المترتبة على الإيمان

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf coordinates يزيد with the syntactic position of falyamdud: God increases the errant in error by abandoning them and increases the guided through divine success.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : يزيد معطوف على موضع فليمدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided incur limited harm followed by immense lasting benefit, while the misguided enjoy limited benefit followed by immense lasting harm, so the former course is plainly better.
rows.anchor: ما عليه المهتدون ضرر قليل متناه يعقبه نفع عظيم غير متناه

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: The investigators identify the enduring good deeds as faith and righteous actions, called enduring because their benefit, their reward, does not cease.
rows.anchor: فقال المحققون إنها الإيمان والأعمال الصالحة سماها باقية لأن نفعها يدوم ولا يبطل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify the enduring deeds as particular acts of worship, naming prayer and, in another view, glorification.
rows.anchor: فبعضهم ذكر الصلوات وبعضهم ذكر التسبيح

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda reports that the Prophet demonstrated that saying the testimony, takbir, and tasbih removes sins like wind strips leaves from a tree; he called these deeds treasures of Paradise.
rows.anchor: جلس رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات يوم وأخذ عودا يابسا

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda said he would perform these words abundantly until an uninformed observer thought him mad.
rows.anchor: وكان أبو الدرداء يقول : لأعلمن ذلك ولأكثرن منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers the comprehensive meaning of faith and all righteous deeds: although deeds vary in reward, all share lasting reward, which makes them enduring and good.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أولى لأنه تعالى إنما وصفها بالباقيات الصالحات من حيث يدوم ثوابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them better in reward and return compares them with what unbelievers claimed was a better dwelling and gathering.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يقال : هذا خير إلا والمراد أنه خير من غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing resurrection and answering deniers, God now recounts their mockery of resurrection.
rows.anchor: اعلم أنه تعالى لما ذكر الدلائل أولا على صحة البعث

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read وُلدا, explained either as a plural of ولد like أُسُد or as a synonym for offspring like عَرَب.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي ولدا وهو جمع ولد كأسد في أسد

rows.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Yaʿmar is reported to read ولد with kasra on the wāw.
rows.anchor: وعن يحيى بن يعمر ولدا بالكسر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the verse was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن نزلت الآية في الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The famous occasion identifies the man as al-As ibn Wa'il; Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said that when he sought repayment, al-As demanded that he disbelieve in Muhammad first.
rows.anchor: والمشهورة أنها في العاص بن وائل ، قال خباب بن الأرت : كان لي عليه دين

rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: In Khabbab's report, al-As asked whether Khabbab believed he would be resurrected; Khabbab affirmed it, and al-As claimed he would then have wealth and children to repay him.
rows.anchor: قلت : نعم . قال : إني بعثت وجئتني فسيكون لي ثم مال وولد فأعطيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate report says Khabbab made jewelry for al-As; when he asked for payment, al-As postponed it, invoking their claim of resurrection and Paradise's gold, silver, and silk.
rows.anchor: وقيل : صاغ خباب له حليا فاقتضاه فطلب الأجرة

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf explains aṭṭalaʿa al-ghayb through ascending a mountain's summit, and says the claimed future could only be reached through unseen knowledge or a covenant with its knower.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : أطلع الغيب من قولهم أطلع الجبل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The covenant is also explained as testimony of faith; Qatada asks whether the claimant had offered a good deed on which to base his expectation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : في العهد كلمة الشهادة عن قتادة هل له عمل صالح قدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes and alerts the claimant that he is mistaken in what he says and hopes for.
rows.anchor: فقال : { كلا } وهي كلمة ردع وتنبيه على الخطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the record is already made, the future tense can mean the claimant will later see and learn that God recorded his words.
rows.anchor: سيظهر له ويعلم أنا كتبنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, future threat language is used for emphasis even when punishment is already underway; the same threatening idiom applies here.
rows.anchor: المتوعد يقول للجاني سوف أنتقم منك وإن كان في الحال في الانتقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will prolong and increase the punishment the man deserves; madda and amadda can both mean to extend it.
rows.anchor: أي نطول له من العذاب ما يستأهله ونزيده من العذاب

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali is reported to read the verb with ḍamma on its initial yāʾ, يمد له.
rows.anchor: ويدل عليه قراءة علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام ويمد له بالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inherits away the wealth and children the man claimed, and the man comes alone in the afterlife, like all people return individually as first created.
rows.anchor: أي يزول عنه ما وعده من مال وولد فلا يعود كما لا يعود الإرث إلى من خلفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters took gods as sources of honor by imagining they would intercede for and support them before God and rescue them from destruction.
rows.anchor: فحكى عنهم أنهم إنما اتخذوا آلهة لأنفسهم ليكونوا لهم عزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rejects their claim to gain honor through the idols.
rows.anchor: وهو ردع لهم وإنكار لتعززهم بالآلهة

rows.speaker: ابن نهيك
rows.claim: Ibn Nuhayk reads the phrase as saying that all of them will disavow worship of the idols.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن نهيك : { كلا سيكفرون بعبادتهم } أي كلهم سيكفرون

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni's al-Muhtasab records a fatḥa-and-tanwīn reading kallan, which he says means the whole belief and opinion is rejected.
rows.anchor: وفي ( محتسب ) ابن جني كلا بفتح الكاف والتنوين وزعم أن معناه

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf says that if this reading is sound, it is the rebuking kallā whose final alif becomes nūn when pausing, as in قواريرا.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : إن صحت هذه الرواية فهي كلا التي هي للردع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes disagree whether the pronoun in سيكفرون refers to the worshipped idols or to their worshippers.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في أن الضمير في قوله : { سيكفرون } يعود إلى المعبود أو إلى العابد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: On one view the referent is the angels: on Judgment Day they disavow worshippers and dispute with them, as in the cited question to those worshipped.
rows.anchor: ثم قال بعضهم : أراد بذلك الملائكة لأنهم في الآخرة يكفرون بعبادتهم

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view is that God resurrects the idols so that they reprimand and disown their worshippers, intensifying the worshippers' regret.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : إن الله تعالى يحيي الأصنام يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: من الناس
rows.claim: A third view refers the pronoun to the worshippers, who will deny that they worshipped idols on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من قال الضمير يرجع إلى العباد أي أن هؤلاء المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being an opposite of honor means disgrace and humiliation, frustrating the purpose for which they adopted the idols; ḍidd can also mean helper.
rows.anchor: والمراد ضد العز وهو الذل والهوان أن يكونون عليهم ضدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although singular, ḍidd describes the plural idols collectively, like the saying that believers are one hand against others, because they are united.
rows.anchor: وحد توحيد قوله عليه السلام : ( وهم يد على من سواهم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols become helpers against their worshippers because they are fuel for Hell and the worshippers are punished for serving them.
rows.anchor: ومعنى كون الآلهة عونا عليهم أنهم وقود النار وحصب جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After discussing idolaters' fate with idols in the afterlife, the passage turns to their obedience to devils in worldly life.
rows.anchor: ذكر بعده حالهم مع الشياطين في الدنيا فإنهم يسألونهم وينقادون لهم

rows.speaker: الأصحاب
rows.claim: The Ashʿari companions argue that sending Satan against unbelievers means God empowered him intending his domination; أز confirms that He intended the incitement, as does the command in another verse.
rows.anchor: احتج الأصحاب بهذه الآية على أن الله تعالى مريد لجميع الكائنات

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi argues that literal sending means dispatching Satan with a message, as prophets are sent; accepting satanic misguidance would then be obedience, an unacceptable implication.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : حقيقة اللفظ توجب أنه تعالى أرسل الشياطين إلى الكفار

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi also says that if God creates and decrees unbelief, Satan can have no causal effect; he therefore interprets sending as God leaving Satan free to mislead, like not restraining one's dog.
rows.anchor: ولأن من العجب تعلق المجبرة بذلك لأن عندهم أن ضلال الكفار من قبله تعالى

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: On the Qadi's interpretation, unbelievers remain able to refuse Satan, and resisting him brings greater reward; the verse of Satan's speech supports their responsibility.
rows.anchor: وهذه التخلية وإن كان فيها تشديد للمحنة عليهم فهم متمكنون من أن لا يقبلوا منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the need to reinterpret: sending against them means empowering Satan over them, not sending him to deliver a message, so the objection confuses two constructions.
rows.anchor: الله تعالى ما أرسل الشياطين إلى الكفار بل أرسلها عليهم والإرسال عليهم هو التسليط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's whisper can produce misguidance in a receptive heart by God's creation, so the resulting error can be attributed to both Satan and God from different aspects.
rows.anchor: إسماع الشيطان إياه تلك الوسوسة يوجب في قلبه ذلك الضلال بشرط سلامة فهم السامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God merely left unbelievers free with devils, He also left them free with prophets; the special mention of Satan must convey an additional point.
rows.anchor: كما خلى بين الشيطان والكفرة فقد خلى بينهم وبين الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because أز means stirring them with force, their agitation is the purpose of the sending, supporting the conclusion that it is willed by God.
rows.anchor: أي تحركهم تحريكا شديدا كالغرض من ذلك الإرسال فوجب أن يكون الأز مرادا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains أزّ as driving or agitating people insistently into sins; he says the verse was revealed about five men who mocked the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { تؤزهم أزا } أي تزعجهم في المعاصي إزعاجا

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf treats azz, hazz, and istifzāz as synonyms for provocation and severe agitation: devils entice people to sins through whispers and insinuations.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : الأز والهز والاستفزاز أخوات في معنى التهييج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not hasten their destruction for relief from their evil: only a limited number of days and breaths remain before the requested end.
rows.anchor: لا تعجل عليهم بأن يهلكوا أو يبيدوا حتى تستريح أنت والمسلمون من شرورهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas would weep at this verse, saying the final count is one's last breath, entry into the grave, and separation from family.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان إذا قرأها بكى وقال : آخر العدد خروج نفسك

rows.speaker: ابن السماك
rows.claim: At al-Ma'mun's court, Ibn al-Sammak said that counted breaths with no extra reserve run out quickly.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن السماك رحمه الله أنه كان عند المأمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God counts their breaths and deeds, requiting both their small and large acts.
rows.anchor: نعد أنفاسهم وأعمالهم فنجازيهم على قليلها وكثيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that God counts the time until each person's fixed lifespan, which cannot be lengthened or shortened.
rows.anchor: نعد الأوقات إلى وقت الأجل المعين لكل أحد

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf parses yawm with an implied verb, either describing God's action toward both groups on that day or commanding the audience to remember it; it may also depend on lā yamlikūn.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : نصب يوم بمضمر أي يوم نحشر ونسوق

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet swore by the One holding his soul that the God-fearing emerge from their graves welcomed on white winged she-camels with golden saddles, then recited the verse.
rows.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi argues that the verse confines the terrors of Judgment to sinners, since the God-fearing are honored from the outset and therefore should not experience terror.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي هذه الآية أحد ما يدل على أن أهوال يوم القيامة تختص بالمجرمين

rows.speaker: المشبهة
rows.claim: The anthropomorphists take إلى الرحمان to mean that the God-fearing movement ends at God; the monotheists understand it as gathering them to the place of God's honor.
rows.anchor: المشبهة احتجوا بالآية وقالوا قوله : { إلى الرحمان } يفيد أن انتهاء حركتهم

rows.speaker: الملحد
rows.claim: An atheist objects that gathering people to God is incoherent if God Himself is the gatherer.
rows.anchor: طعن الملحد فيه فقال قوله : { يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمان وفدا }

rows.speaker: المسلمون
rows.claim: Muslims answer the atheist by supplying the sense: God gathers the God-fearing to His honor.
rows.anchor: أجاب المسلمون بأن التقدير يوم نحشر المتقين إلى كرامة الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb نسوق conveys that criminals are driven toward Hell in humiliation, like thirsty livestock herded to water.
rows.anchor: فقوله : { نسوق } يدل على أنهم يساقون إلى النار بإهانة واستخفاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ward means thirsty people because those who come to water do so from thirst; more literally, it is travel to water, then the word names those arriving.
rows.anchor: والورد اسم للعطاش ، لأن من يرد الماء لا يرده إلا للعطش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpreters disagree whether the people in question cannot intercede for others or whether nobody else can intercede for them.
rows.anchor: فلذلك اختلفوا ، وقال بعضهم : لا يملكون أن يشفعوا لغيرهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One interpretation is that they cannot intercede for others as believers can.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لا يملكون أن يشفعوا لغيرهم كما يملك المؤمنون

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The other interpretation is that no one else can intercede for them.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : بل المراد لا يملك غيرهم أن يشفعوا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers the second reading because the first merely states an obvious point; the covenant exception then shows that those with faith and prophethood may receive intercession, including grave sinners.
rows.anchor: وهذا الثاني أولى لأن حمل الآية على الأول يجري مجرى إيضاع الواضحات

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet taught a daily morning and evening covenant affirming God's oneness and Muhammad's messengership, asking for mercy and protection from one's own self; God seals it beneath the Throne and its holders are called into Paradise on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: ما روى ابن مسعود أنه عليه السلام قال لأصحابه ذات يوم : ( أيعجز أحدكم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi says the verse supports his doctrine, while Razi concludes that it strongly supports their view of intercession for grave sinners.
rows.anchor: وقال القاضي : الآية دالة على مذهبه وقد ظهر أن الآية قوية في الدلالة على قولنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After refuting idol worship, the passage rejects those who claim God has a child: Jews say Ezra is God's son, Christians say the Messiah, and Arabs say angels are God's daughters.
rows.anchor: وقالت اليهود * عزيز * ابن الله وقالت النصارى المسيح ابن الله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some restrict these verses to Arabs who claimed the angels were God's daughters, since the surah already answered the Christians earlier and now turns from Arab idolaters to angel worship.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من خصها بالعرب الذي أثبتوا أن الملائكة بنات الله

rows.speaker: ابن خالويه
rows.claim: Ibn Khalawayh says idd and add mean something astonishing; another explanation calls it a grave abomination, while addah can mean hardship.
rows.anchor: قال ابن خالويه الإد والأد العجب وقيل المنكر العظيم والأدة الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recitation of yatafattarna varies in its initial consonant: some read the verb with yāʾ, others with tāʾ; Ibn Masud reads yataṣaddaʿna.
rows.anchor: قرىء يتفطرن بالتاء بعد الياء أعني المعجمة من تحتها واختلفوا في يكاد

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud's reading is يتصدعن.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود يتصدعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infiṭār is splitting; tafaṭṭur intensifies the sense by repeating or doubling the action.
rows.anchor: والانفطار من فطرة إذا شقه والتفطر من فطره إذا شققه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about mountains crashing can mean they crash violently, are crushed, or crash because they are being crushed; the image is of their strongest collapse onto one another.
rows.anchor: أي تهد هدا أو مهدودة أو مفعول له أي لأنها تهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that God would make the heavens, earth, and mountains rupture in anger at this utterance if His forbearance did not delay punishment.
rows.anchor: أن الله سبحانه وتعالى يقول أفعل هذا بالسموات والأرض والجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation magnifies the claim's enormity and portrays its destructive effect on religion and its foundations.
rows.anchor: أن يكون استعظاما للكلمة وتهويلا من فظاعتها وتصويرا لأثرها في الدين

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says the heavens and earth would nearly rupture if they could understand the enormity of this claim.
rows.anchor: وهذا تأويل أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth explanation says the heavens, earth, and mountains had been free of defects until human beings voiced this claim.
rows.anchor: أن السموات والأرض والجبال كانت سليمة من كل العيوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase أَن دعوا has three parses: genitive as an appositive to the pronoun in منه, accusative with an omitted lām, or nominative as the subject of هدا; each makes the claim the cause of the cosmic rupture.
rows.anchor: في إعرابه ثلاثة أوجه . أحدها : أن يكون مجرورا بدلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating al-Rahman emphasizes that God alone is the source of every blessing, both its foundations and its branches.
rows.anchor: إنما كرر لفظ الرحمن مرات تنبيها على أنه سبحانه وتعالى هو الرحمن وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes daʿaw as naming, normally with two objects but with one retained to encompass everyone to whom a child is ascribed.
rows.anchor: هو من دعا بمعنى سمى المتعدي إلى مفعولين فاقتصر على أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, daʿaw means to attribute lineage, as in the hadith phrase about someone claiming descent from other than his patrons.
rows.anchor: أو من دعا بمعنى نسب الذي هو مطاوعة ما في قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( من ادعى إلى غير مواليه )

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet's line إنا بني نهشل لا ندعى لأب illustrates not being affiliated by descent to a father.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر :
إنا بني نهشل لا ندعى لأب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking a child is impossible for God: physical birth is plainly impossible, and adoption is impossible because a child must resemble its parent, while nothing resembles God.
rows.anchor: أما الولادة المعروفة فلا مقال في امتناعها ، وأما التبني فلأن الولد لا بد وأن يكون شبيها بالوالد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human reasons for adopting a child—joy, assistance, or a good name—cannot apply to God.
rows.anchor: ولأن اتخاذ الولد إنما يكون لأغراض لا تصح في الله من سروره به واستعانته به وذكر جميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every worshipped being in heaven and earth, including angels and people, returns to God as a submissive, humble servant who hopes in Him.
rows.anchor: والمراد أنه ما من معبود لهم في السموات والأرض من الملائكة والناس إلا وهو يأتي

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some restrict the statement about every being coming as a servant to the Day of Judgment; Razi prefers the unrestricted reading because it needs no restriction.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من حمله على يوم القيامة خاصة والأول أولى لأنه لا تخصيص فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has counted and numbered them all: they remain under His command, governance, power, and control, and He knows their general and particular affairs without missing anything.
rows.anchor: أي كلهم تحت أمره وتدبيره وقهره وقدرته فهو سبحانه ميحط بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person comes alone on Judgment Day, without the alleged partners, who disown the idolaters.
rows.anchor: وكل واحد منهم يأتيه يوم القيامة منفردا ليس معه من هؤلاء المشركين أحد
